comments.author: @coryfeco9348
comments.text:
Actually, since the comic is in English it is implied that items would be written on the board from left to right.... 

This means that the square would have been written first.... revealing.... to the other 2 parties that they were indeed thinking of 3 different items.

Granted the full epiphany that all 3 parties were thinking different shapes would happen upon the 3rd member drawing the 3rd object.

However, given the positioning I think we can all agree that it was very likely that each character was below their corresponding shape.

Otherwise the comic writer would have moved the characters into different positions, as demonstrated by their colors, if they wanted to show the act of moving to draw on the chalk board.

Is it possible that party 2 or 3 went first yes. However given the way comics read, English is written, and people in English speaking countries act given the above, it would be illogical to assume otherwise without the writer of the comic presenting additional evidence.

This means that once the square was revealed it illuminated the concept of their false share understanding with one another.

Granted there was clearly an inclination of misunderstanding, or they wouldn't gone through the act of visualizing what they had in mind, but I would argue the Ai understood the tipping point was at moment the square was drawn and the other two characters observed the 1st's results. 

This means that not only did Ai get it right, but it potentially understood the series of events far better than those debating the contrary.

I think it's important to note this means that not only was the Ai likely not wrong, it was also arguably smarter than anyone who didn't immediately intuit that. 😮
